purpose: Independent fixed-budget ABACA check after the six-control CPU calibration narrowly missed its declared accuracy criterion on this case.

selection.reason: Original 64-repetition CPU result: estimated loss error 0.005314211380881062 bits; absolute error plus 95% interval halfwidth 0.010028366546684708 bits against the unchanged 0.01-bit threshold.
selection.fixed_budget: 128 fresh repetitions at 16384 particles; complete the whole batch and assess once. Preserve all results regardless of outcome.
selection.independence: Master seed 2026091650 differs from all original CPU stages and the GPU benchmark. Each global repetition index 0..127 receives a distinct derived seed.
selection.old_records: Original six-case calibration, including failed ABACA, stays unchanged. The other five controls are reused in the comparison. Do not pool estimates across the two particle counts.

comparison.method: Independently validate both complete receipts and recompute their statistics from raw repetitions. Keep original and new ABACA estimates separate; list which receipt supports each of the six controls.
comparison.scope: A short-control diagnostic. It does not modify or automatically satisfy original-stage prerequisites, authorize production references, or validate long sequences.

limitations: The case and follow-up effort were chosen after observing the original failure; this is disclosed numerical calibration, not untouched confirmation of the source-learning claim.
The approximate 95% Monte Carlo interval does not bound discretization bias or missed modes.
Quadrature refinement and broader confirmation remain separate future checks.
Standalone requires=[] makes this independently executable; it does not change any gate in the original plan.
